correctness.rationale: Let n=ord(q^2) be even, q+q^{-1} != 0, and t=q^(n^2), exactly as in the cited source. Proposition 5.2 gives a complex vector-space basis consisting of the unit/empty diagram, w and unoriented loop classes e_[u], u in Z^2\{0} modulo ±. Theorem 5.6, using Lemma 5.5, gives Fr(empty)=empty, Fr(w)=0 and Fr(e_[u])=e_[nu]. Since multiplication by nonzero n induces an injection on the ±-quotient of the lattice, the non-w images are a linearly independent subset of the target basis. Every skein has a FINITE linear expansion; hence its image vanishes precisely if its unit and every loop coefficient vanish, with w arbitrary. This proves ker Fr=Cw. The package proof implicitly needs canonical representatives for ± labels; making that indexing convention explicit resolves the harmless ambiguity without modifying the theorem.
residual_risks: Proof depends on the published torus basis and full Frobenius action as source theorems; their skein calculations were not independently reproved.
Unoriented indices ± must be normalized to distinct basis classes; the assigned finite sum tacitly assumes this.
n=2 is excluded by q+q^{-1} != 0, and no extension to other surfaces or different specialization is proved.

value.rationale: The dimension of the kernel of a naturally defined Frobenius map is a meaningful structural quantity, and identifying a minimal loss of injectivity could be useful in a new setting. Here, however, the supplied contribution is only the immediate linear-algebra extraction from an already complete published basis-action table: all the challenging skein construction, basis independence and parity computation occur in the source. No new structural lemma, quotient presentation, previously uncomputable invariant, or motivated nontrivial boundary is established. The exact fact is mechanically implied by stronger known data, so its isolated restatement does not meet the stipulated independent mathematical-value bar.
residual_risks: A short corollary recording the precise kernel may be pedagogically useful to readers; that utility is not the same as a distinct research contribution.
A substantive quotient-algebra or other-surface computation might change value, but none is supplied or asserted by the actual final claim.
